title: Nudge-token whitelist is registration-time-only; collectNudge never re-checks it, so SYA keeps donating into a sink that can no longer distribute
fingerprintBasis: sha256(src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:claim:registration-time-only-whitelist-invariant-decays-on-value-path-donor-keeps-donating-into-non-distributing-sink)  [entryPoint null -> legacy hash form, byte-identical to pre-entryPoint findings]
description: While the condition persists, claimer-paid nudge value accumulates as (a) a streamer buffer that has lost its flusher and (b) dead balance already settled into the sink that batchMint will no longer iterate. Both pools are RECOVERED in full by re-whitelisting the token — nothing is destroyed.
impact: Value PAUSED, not leaked -- both pools are recovered in full by re-whitelisting. Claims keep SUCCEEDING with no revert and no event on the SYA side. DETECTION is the weak link, not recovery.
attackPath: 1. NudgeStreamer.registerStream enforces isNudgeToken(token) on the batch minter (NudgeStreamer.sol:112-114) — the structural 'this sink can actually distribute this token' guard.
2. collectNudge (:137-156) does NOT re-check it, and neither does SYA.
3. The BatchNFTMinterMultiToken owner calls setNudgeTokenWhitelist(USDC, false) — e.g. rotating the reward pot. The token leaves _nudgeTokens (swap-and-pop).

4. SYA's claims keep succeeding and keep pushing USDC into the streamer and, via _settle, into the sink's balance. But batchMint's step-3.5 flush loops _nudgeTokens, which no longer contains USDC, so the streamer buffer loses its flusher; and batchMint no longer iterates USDC, so the settled balance sits undistributed.
recommendation: Have NudgeStreamer.collectNudge re-assert isNudgeToken so the value path fails loud, or expose an owner-callable flush on NudgeStreamer keyed by (batchMinter, token). SYA-side interim: emit or revert if a pre-claim probe of the sink's whitelist fails. Root cause is arguably in phoenix-nft-staking; filed here because SYA is the donor that keeps the flow alive after the invariant breaks.
law3Ruling: IN SCOPE as a non-obvious footgun: an owner de-whitelisting a token would not expect it to silently strand an active donor's ongoing flow.
residualAggravator: The silence is real and survives the downgrade: SYA emits nothing and reverts nothing, so detection depends on someone noticing batchMint has stopped paying out that token. Recovery is cheap; DETECTION is the weak link.

validity.rescope: First-party framing is DONOR-SIDE: SYA is the contract that KEEPS DONATING into a sink that can no longer distribute after the owner de-whitelists. The missing re-check inside collectNudge is upstream (phoenix-nft-staking) and is ROUTED as the recommended cure, not filed as an SYA defect.

rationaleAmendment: SHARED-OWNERSHIP CLAUSE STRUCK from the rationale per the severity revision. The finding stands on the donor leg alone; do not lean on the same-operator-on-both-sides argument.
